title: Soldering Copper Pipe: Prep, Flux, and Torch Technique
summary: This This Old House segment demonstrates essential copper-pipe soldering prep and execution. It covers cleaning copper surfaces with Emery cloth and a cleaning brush, applying flux to both pipe and fitting, choosing and using a basic heat torch with two tip styles, and performing a heat-and-solder sequence that relies on capillary action to draw solder into the joint. The video also flags important safety notes: ensuring the old piping is dry before soldering and using a heat shield when working near wood to avoid fire hazards.
topics: Hottest part of flame at the tip
Heat one side of the fitting
Apply solder to opposite side of flame
Heat draws solder into joint (capillary action)
Remove flame while solder is still liquid
Dry piping to prevent solder failure
Avoiding fire when working around wood

sections.title: Surface cleaning: copper pipe and fitting
concepts: Emery cloth cleaning of exterior pipe
Emery cloth cleaning of fitting interior
sections.description: Begin by cleaning copper surfaces with Emery cloth on both the pipe exterior and the fitting interior to promote solder bonding; a cleaning brush is introduced for longer life.

sections.title: Flux application to pipe and fitting
sections.description: Apply flux to both the pipe and the fitting before heating to promote solder flow and coverage.

sections.title: Torch overview and tip options
sections.description: The torch is described as having two parts (fuel canister and tip). It contrasts a basic pencil-tip torch that must be ignited manually with a smaller flame to a larger-tip torch with built-in spark ignition for higher heat.

sections.title: Heat control and solder application prep
concepts: Heat one side of the fitting
Solder application from the opposite side of the flame
sections.description: Apply heat to one side of the fitting long enough for flux to bubble; then apply solder to the opposite side of the flame so the heat draws the solder into the joint by capillary action.

sections.title: Safety reminders: dry piping and heat shielding
concepts: Solder will not melt if water is present
Heat shield near wood to prevent fire
sections.description: If working with old piping, ensure the pipe is free of water; when near wood, use a heat shield to prevent fire hazards.
